title: Year 9 Science Test 1
topics: Biology (40%): variation, adaptation, natural selection, cells · Chemistry (20%): states of matter, atoms · Physics (40%): units, density, forces, energy, speed
weighting_note: Agreed with Albert, November 2026: the paper is split by time, 40% biology, 20% chemistry, 40% physics. At one mark a minute that is 16, 8 and 16 marks of the 40.
instructions: You have 40 minutes. There are three parts: Biology (16 marks), Chemistry (8 marks) and Physics (16 marks). Answer all the questions.
Spend about one minute on each mark: 16 minutes on Biology, 8 minutes on Chemistry and 16 minutes on Physics.
The last question in each part is harder (Stretch and Challenge). Answer the other questions in that part first.
Write your answers in the spaces on this paper. The marks for each part of a question are shown in brackets, for example [2].

sections.title: Part 1: Biology
sections.subject: biology
sections.intro: Questions 1 to 5 are Core. Question 6 is Stretch and Challenge.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Put one tick in each row to show whether the factor is abiotic (non-living) or biotic (living).
parts.answer: temperature: abiotic; predation: biotic; amount of light: abiotic; infectious disease: biotic. All four correct = 2 marks; two or three correct = 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Which one of these shows continuous variation? Tick one box.
parts.answer: height

parts.label: a
parts.text: Complete the sentences using words from the box. One word is not needed.
gaps: Genetic information is stored in the ______________________ of a cell.
A sperm cell and an egg cell join together at ______________________ to make a zygote.
parts.answer: nucleus (1), fertilisation (1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Draw one line from each way of protecting a species to how it works.

right: endangered animals are bred in captivity to increase their numbers
seeds, gametes or cells are stored at a low temperature
an area where the habitat and the species living in it are protected

parts.answer: nature reserve: an area where the habitat and the species living in it are protected; breeding programme: endangered animals are bred in captivity; gene bank: seeds, gametes or cells stored at a low temperature. All three correct = 2 marks; one correct = 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In the 1800s, black peppered moths became more common near Manchester. The sentences below explain why, but they are in the wrong order. Write 1, 2, 3 and 4 in the boxes to put them in the correct order.

rows: Birds spotted and ate more pale moths than black moths.
A few moths had genes that made them black.
Each generation had more black moths than the one before.
Soot from factories made the tree trunks black.

parts.answer: Correct order: a few moths had genes that made them black (1); soot made the tree trunks black (2); birds ate more pale moths (3); each generation had more black moths (4). All four correct = 2 marks; first and last correct = 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The diagram shows a plant cell. Write the name of each labelled part.
parts.answer: A cell wall, B nucleus, C chloroplast, D vacuole. All four correct = 2 marks; two or three correct = 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A microscope has a x10 eyepiece lens and a x4 objective lens. Calculate the total magnification.

parts.label: a
parts.text: By 1895 most peppered moths near Manchester were black, because soot from factories had made the tree trunks black. Since the 1960s the air has been much cleaner. There is very little soot, and the tree trunks are pale again.

sub.text: Predict what has happened to the numbers of black moths and pale moths near Manchester since the 1960s.
Explain your prediction. Use the idea of natural selection.

parts.answer: (i) The number of black moths has gone down and the number of pale moths has gone up (1). (ii) On pale tree trunks the pale moths are better camouflaged, so birds spot and eat more black moths (1). More pale moths survive and reproduce (1). They pass on their genes, so each generation has more pale moths (1). Do not credit 'the moths changed colour'.

sections.title: Part 2: Chemistry
sections.subject: chemistry
sections.intro: Questions 7 and 8 are Core. Question 9 is Stretch and Challenge.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The diagrams show the particles in a solid, a liquid and a gas. Write solid, liquid or gas for each diagram.
parts.answer: A gas, B solid, C liquid. All three correct = 2 marks; one or two correct = 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A sodium atom has atomic number 11 and mass number 23.

sub.text: How many protons does the atom have?
How many neutrons does the atom have?

parts.answer: (i) 11 protons (1). (ii) 23 - 11 = 12 neutrons (1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: A sodium atom has 11 electrons. Complete its electron configuration.
parts.answer: 2,8,1 (the missing number is 1).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Use your answer to part (b). Which group of the periodic table is sodium in? Tick one box.
parts.answer: group 1 (one electron in the outer shell).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Fluorine (atomic number 9) and chlorine (atomic number 17) are both in group 7 of the periodic table.

sub.text: Write the electron configuration of each atom.
Explain why fluorine and chlorine react in similar ways.

parts.answer: (i) fluorine 2,7 and chlorine 2,8,7, both correct (1). (ii) Both have seven electrons in the outer shell, and the outer electrons decide how an element reacts (1).

sections.title: Part 3: Physics
sections.subject: physics
sections.intro: Questions 10 to 14 are Core. Question 15 is Stretch and Challenge. Most of these questions come from the physics revision guide.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the SI units (name and symbol) of the following quantities.
parts.answer: length: metre, m (1). volume: cubic metre, m³ (1). Give the mark only if the name and the symbol are both right. Do not accept cm³, mm³ or litres, which are not SI units.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Read question 1 in the picture. Use the table. Write the letter of the correct answer.
parts.answer: D. The cubes have the same volume, so each pushes aside the same volume of water and the level rises by the same amount.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Read question 2 in the picture. Use the table above. Write the letter of the correct answer.
parts.answer: B (silver). The masses are the same, so the metal with the lowest density has the largest volume and makes the biggest rise. Silver has the lowest density, 10.49 g/cm³.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A skydiver is falling at a steady speed. Name the upward force on the skydiver.
parts.answer: air resistance (accept drag)

parts.label: b
parts.text: The skydiver's speed is not changing. Are the forces on the skydiver balanced or unbalanced? Tick one box.
parts.answer: balanced

parts.label: a
parts.text: Complete the law of conservation of energy. Write one word in each gap.
gaps: It can only be ______________________ from one store to another.
parts.answer: created (1), destroyed (1), in either order; transferred (1). Accept transformed for the third mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use the picture. Write the letter of the correct answer.
parts.answer: A. Machine Y wastes 11 J out of 20 J, much less of its energy than machine X, which wastes 91 J out of 100 J. Its efficiency is 9 ÷ 20 = 45%, against 9% for X.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The distance-time graph shows a cyclist's ride. How far did the cyclist travel? Tick one box.
parts.answer: C (3.5 miles): the line ends at 3.5 miles on the distance axis.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Draw an X on the part of the graph where the cyclist was travelling at the fastest speed.
parts.answer: An X on the first section of the line, from 0 to 10 minutes. It is the steepest, with 2 miles in 10 minutes. Do not accept an X on any other section.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Answer the question in the picture. Write your answers on the lines.
parts.answer: (i) 15.8 g, from 0.79 × 20.00 (1). (ii) 15.9 cm³, from 20.00 ÷ 1.26 = 15.87; accept 15.8 or 15.9 (1). (iii) 0.90 g/cm³, from 25.90 ÷ 28.80 = 0.899; accept 0.89 or 0.90 (1). (iv) 0.85 g/cm³, from 30.00 ÷ 35.30 = 0.850 (1). The units are printed on the paper, so do not penalise a missing unit.
gaps: i   Mass of the ethanol = ______________ g
ii   Volume of the glycerin = ______________ cm³
iii   Density of the olive oil = ______________ g/cm³
iv   Density of the turpentine = ______________ g/cm³
